findings.title: Schema's required keys and field types are not stated
findings.detail: Goals say a `category` on "every finding", and `ADVERSARIAL_REVIEWER_SCHEMA` lists `category`, `trigger` and `lines` per finding. The spec never says which of these are `required`. CONFORMANCE_REVIEWER_SCHEMA (personas.py:78) requires only `severity` and `title`. The spec also doesn't give `lines`' type (array of ints, strings, or ranges?). Say that `category` is required and the enum is closed, that `trigger` is optional (a missing trigger caps severity at `minor`, enforced by prompt only), and give the type of `lines`. Otherwise the schema AC ("category enum, trigger") can't be checked objectively.

findings.title: `trigger` and `lines` are dropped from the ledger and nothing says so
findings.detail: `_events_for_result` (queue.py:373-378) copies only ac/title/detail/files, and the spec adds only `category`. `trigger` and `lines` (cite file and line) exist only in the persisted `last_review.verdicts` state. If they should reach the ledger or the implementer's `fix_brief`, say so. If not, state that it is deliberate. Also note that SPEC-0201 line 255 says `_events_for_result` "already handles the shape", while this spec says it must be changed to copy `category`. Reconcile the two statements.

findings.title: Docs update is promised but no criterion covers it
findings.detail: Design says the capability page "Reviews" lists the three reviewers and their categories. No acceptance criterion or Definition-of-done item checks this. Add a criterion (for example `docs/product/capabilities/agentic.md` lists the three reviewers and the category set), or drop the bullet.

findings.title: "`pass` with a `must_fix` is `fix`" has no explicit test
findings.detail: The Design states this rule. It is enforced by SPEC-0201's `combine_reviews`, and the e2e paths listed here use a `must_fix` finding. No test is named for an adversarial verdict of `pass` that carries a `must_fix` finding. Add it to the e2e or queue test list.

findings.title: Default cap impact is not analysed
findings.detail: With balanced's default cap of 10.0 and an implementer budget of 4.0, reviewers now cost up to 1.5+1.0+1.5 = 4.0 per pass, where they cost 1.5 today. If budgets are spent in full, a second fix loop would park on `cost_cap` at the implementer step (4+4+4 > 10). SPEC-0201 analyses the cap for two reviewers. State here whether `campaign_cap_usd` defaults stay unchanged for three reviewers, and what happens at the worst-case spend.
